nodes.name: CoMo2S4 synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.01 g molybdenum powder was completely dissolved in 10 mL H2O2 (3%) at 60 °C. Then, 0.01286 g cobalt acetylacetone (II) was added to the solution. After cobalt acetylacetone (II) was completely dissolved, 1.4 mL solution was transferred to a saturated sodium chloride solution containing sodium chloride solid, and the mixed solution was freeze-dried in vacuum for 12 h. After that, the obtained dry solid was vulcanized at high temperature: thiourea was served as sulfur source, and the vulcanization process was carried out in nitrogen atmosphere at 400 °C for 2 h.

nodes.description: HER performance evaluation in 1 M NaOH
nodes.source_text: The electrochemical test is carried out in a three-electrode electrolytic cell, in which the counter electrode is platinum plate electrode, the reference electrode is Ag/AgCl electrode, and the working electrode is a carbon cloth electrode loaded with CoMo₂S₄ catalyst. The electrolyte used in the test is 1 M NaOH... All electrochemical measurements were performed under identical conditions with the same catalyst mass loading (0.65 mg cm⁻²)... HER polarization curves were recorded with the scan rate of 10 mV s⁻¹... LSV test results show that the overpotential of CoMo₂S₄ at the current density of 10 and 100 mA cm⁻² is 55 and 150 mV, respectively... the exchange current of CoMo₂S₄ is 0.74 mA cm⁻²... the Tafel value of CoMo₂S₄ is 84.61 mV dec⁻¹... Stability test is carried out at current density of 100 mA cm⁻² for 24 h, and the HER overpotential of CoMo₂S₄ only increases by 8 mV.

nodes.description: HER performance after H₂O₂ shielding test
nodes.source_text: It is found that the HER performance of CoMo₂S₄ decreased significantly after being treated by 5% H₂O₂, implying Mo as the main active site.

nodes.description: HER performance after HCl shielding test
nodes.source_text: However, in contrast, after 5% HCl shielding, the HER performance of CoMo₂S₄ does not decrease significantly, which means that Co is not the main active site.

nodes.description: HER performance vs film thickness on FTO
nodes.source_text: In contrast, for CoMo₂S₄ and CoS₂, no significant decrease is found in HER performance as the number of layer increases from 1 to 6, suggesting superior charge transfer within CoMo₂S₄.

nodes.description: HER performance vs film thickness on FTO
nodes.source_text: Apparently, the HER performance of MoS₂ decreases significantly as the film thickness increases. Specifically, the overpotential of MoS₂ increases (from 0.35 to 0.53 V) at 10 mA cm⁻² as the number of layer increases from 1 to 6.

nodes.description: HER performance vs film thickness on FTO
nodes.source_text: In contrast, for CoMo₂S₄ and CoS₂, no significant decrease is found in HER performance as the number of layer increases from 1 to 6.

nodes.description: HER benchmark performance in 1 M NaOH
nodes.source_text: To make a fair comparison, the linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves shown in this work are compensated by the iR compensation... the overpotential of CoMo₂S₄ at 10 mA cm⁻² is closed to that of Pt/C (20%) with a difference of 56 mV. Notably, when the current density is greater than 50 mA cm⁻², the HER performance of CoMo₂S₄ is obviously superior to that of Pt/C (20%). Particularly, the HER overpotential of CoMo₂S₄ is 59.6 mV lower than that of Pt/C (20%) at the current density of 100 mA cm⁻²... exchange current of Pt/C (20%) (0.69 mA cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks at 29.305°, 32.459°, 34.762°, 43.871°, and 48.750° match the (−313), (311), (−404), (−132), and (511) crystal faces of standard monoclinic CoMo₂S₄ (PDF:71-0378).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD test result (Figure 1a) shows that the diffraction peaks (at 29.305°, 32.459°, 34.762°, 43.871°, and 48.750°) of the as-synthesized material match well with the (−313), (311), (−404), (−132), and (511) crystal faces of standard CoMo₂S₄ (PDF:71-0378), preliminarily suggesting that monoclinic CoMo₂S₄ phase of the as-synthesized material.

nodes.characterization_summary: Reveals 2D nanosheet morphology of the catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and atomic force microscope (AFM) are performed to test and analyze the morphology and structure of the material.
The tests results reveal that the morphology of the as-synthesized material is a 2D nanosheet structure (Figure 1b), of which the thickness is ≈5 nm (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Distance between E'₂g and A₁g peaks is 22.53 cm⁻¹, smaller than bulk CoMo₂S₄ (32.54 cm⁻¹), confirming thin 2D structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman test further confirms the thin structure of the as-synthesized 2D CoMo₂S₄. The distance between the E'₂g and A₁g peaks in 2D CoMo₂S₄ (22.53 cm⁻¹) is smaller than that in bulk CoMo₂S₄ (32.54 cm⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Shows thin 2D nanosheet structure consistent with SEM and AFM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image shows that the morphology structure of the material is a thin 2D nanosheet structure (Figure 1d), which is consistent with the results of SEM and AFM tests.

nodes.characterization_summary: Shows two diffraction rings with d-spacing of 2.76 Å and 1.65 Å, corresponding to (311) and (134) crystal faces of CoMo₂S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the corresponding SAED of the multilayered stacked nanosheets shows two diffraction rings with the d-spacing of 2.76 and 1.65 Å, respectively, corresponding to (311) and (134) crystal faces of CoMo₂S₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: Reveals regular lattice matrix in 2D nanosheet with (311) and (134) crystal faces (d-spacings 2.76 Å and 1.65 Å) at 47° angle, confirming monoclinic phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM test reveals a regular lattice matrix in the 2D nanosheet (Figure 1e; Figure S3, Supporting Information). By in-depth analyzing the lattice matrix with different directions, it can be found (311) and (134) crystal faces with d-spacing of 2.76 and 1.65 Å, respectively, which is consistent with the SAED results.

nodes.characterization_summary: Shows uniform distribution of Co, Mo, and S elements along the 2D nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) mapping (Figure 1f) test result shows that the elements of Co, Mo, and S are uniformly distributed along the 2D nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p binding energies at 778.8 eV (2p₃/₂) and 793.7 eV (2p₁/₂) indicate Co–S bond closer to metallic Co; Mo 3d at 229.0 eV (3d₅/₂) and 232.1 eV (3d₃/₂) for Mo–S; S 2p at 161.8 eV (2p₃/₂) and 163.0 eV (2p₁/₂) for metal–S; ΔE (Co 2p₃/₂–S 2p₃/₂) = 617 eV confirms CoMo₂S₄ phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co 2p XPS test result shows that the binding energy of Co in CoMo₂S₄ mainly centers at 778.8 eV (Co 2p₃/₂) and 793.7 eV (Co 2p₁/₂)... For the Co–Mo–S synthesized in this work, the ΔE value is determined to be 617 eV, further indicating that the synthesized Co–Mo–S material is CoMo₂S₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: Resistivity of CoMo₂S₄ is 0.34 kΩ cm, MoS₂ is 3.15 kΩ cm, and CoS₂ is 0.44 kΩ cm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The resistivity (Figure 5b) of CoMo₂S₄ is determined to be 0.34 kΩ cm, which is almost one order of magnitude lower than that of MoS₂ (3.15 kΩ cm).

nodes.characterization_summary: Rs of CoMo₂S₄ is 2.2 Ω, MoS₂ is 3.0 Ω, CoS₂ is 2.6 Ω.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S21 in the Supporting Information, the Rs of CoMo₂S₄ is 2.2 Ω while the Rs for MoS₂ and CoS₂ is 3.0 and 2.6 Ω, respectively.
